topic: Bayes' Theorem: The Geometry of Changing Your Mind
target_audience: University students and lifelong learners with a basic grasp of probability

sections.title: The Prior: Setting the Stage
lecture_lines: This unit square represents our entire sample space.
We divide it to represent different possible outcomes.
Ten percent represent rare Golden Squirrels, others are Grey.
These areas show the initial probability of each group.
This gold strip is our prior belief for Golden Squirrels.
animations: Create a unit square (side length 4) with a white outline (#FFFFFF) and label it 'Sample Space' below.
Draw a vertical line at 10% width from the left edge of the square.
Fill the left 10% strip with gold (#FFD700) and the remaining 90% with grey (#808080).
Animate the text labels 'P(Gold)=0.1' and 'P(Grey)=0.9' appearing in the strips.
Apply a pulsing white (#FFFFFF) stroke to the gold strip's border.

sections.title: The Evidence Filter (Likelihood)
lecture_lines: A camera glints when detecting a squirrel's presence.
We shade areas where the camera triggers a glint.
These heights represent the likelihood of observing a glint.
animations: Draw a horizontal line at 80% height in the gold strip and 20% height in the grey strip.
Color the top-left area bright yellow (#FFFACD) and the top-right area light grey (#D3D3D3).
Display 'P(Glint|Gold)=0.8' and 'P(Glint|Grey)=0.2' labels near the shaded areas.

sections.title: The Geometry of New Information
lecture_lines: When the camera glints, non-glinting outcomes become impossible.
We focus only on the regions where evidence occurred.
The rest of the sample space is now discarded.
animations: Animate the bottom 20% of the gold strip and bottom 80% of the grey strip turning dark grey (#222222).
Create a bold white (#FFFFFF) outline around the top-left and top-right shaded areas.
Fade out all labels from the previous step, leaving only the shaded rectangles and their new borders.

sections.title: Normalizing the Space (The Posterior)
lecture_lines: Let's combine the remaining areas to form a new space.
This total area represents all possible glinting events.
We normalize this space back into a unit square.
The gold region's relative size gives the new probability.
This updated value is called the posterior probability.
animations: Translate the gold-glint and grey-glint rectangles to the center, side-by-side, removing gaps.
Add a white (#FFFFFF) brace at the bottom spanning both rectangles, labeled 'Total Evidence: 0.26'.
Scale the grouped rectangles to occupy a 4x4 area, filling the original square's space.
Show the math text '0.08 / 0.26 ≈ 31%' appearing centered in the now-larger gold section.
Change the label of the gold section to 'Posterior P(Gold|Glint)' in gold text (#FFD700).

sections.title: The Bayesian Formula: From Shapes to Algebra
lecture_lines: These geometric steps form the famous Bayes' Theorem formula.
The gold term represents our initial prior belief.
The yellow term is the likelihood from our evidence.
We divide by the total probability of the evidence.
This formula elegantly captures how we update our knowledge.
animations: Transform the visual areas into the text 'P(A|B) = [P(B|A)P(A)] / P(B)' in the center of the screen.
Color the 'P(A)' term gold (#FFD700) to match the initial strip color.
Color the 'P(B|A)' term bright yellow (#FFFACD) to match the likelihood height color.
Color the denominator 'P(B)' white (#FFFFFF) and highlight it with an underline.
Apply a final pulsing glow to the entire formula in white (#FFFFFF).
